name: calendar.created: an event already on the calendar is no candidate even when it outscores the new one
notes: Sprint 1 close (TECH-R4): written from docs/grading.md alone, so that a cross-check reading every observation in the window, without the §4.1 calendar.created first-seen rule, disagrees with the contract. 52 and 83 exclude a pre-existing event only where no other candidate exists (score null); here the excluded event is the better match.

c1 (muse, calendar.created, 'Q3 review', claimed 14:02, minute precision, targetAt Thu 10-08 14:00): window targetAt ± calendarDays 3 = [10-05 14:00, 10-11 14:00] (§4.1). A subject-only calendar claim: applicable timeProximity 2500, subjectOverlap 1500; Σw = 4000 (§5.2; the counterparty features need a claim counterparty). The grant binds gcal.event to acct-a; two passes (acct-a, all calendars) saw [10-01, 11-01], synced 09:00 and 14:40.

First-seen (§4.1 v1.3): a calendar.created candidate needs the earliest observedAt of its contentHash group ≥ start(p,t) − beforeClaimMin = 14:02 − 2 min = 14:00. o1 'Q3 review' at 10-08 14:00 was first seen at 09:00 (stated) < 14:00: it was already on the calendar → not a candidate. o2 'Q3 review prep' at 10-08 14:00 (another contentHash) was first seen at 14:40 (stated; the loader default would be the 09:00 pass, before the event existed) ≥ 14:00 → a candidate.

c1 × o2: Δ = 0 from targetAt → tp 1; subject {q3, review} vs {q3, review, prep} → 2/3. S = (2500 + 1500·2/3)/4000 = 3500/4000 = 7/8. Verified: 10000·3500 = 35 000 000 ≥ 8500·4000 = 34 000 000 → VERIFIED, o2 assigned.

Coverage full (both entries eligible, bound, allCalendars, and [10-01, 11-01] ⊇ the window), so no_coverage does not fire first. State (§8): VERIFIED is FINAL once an eligible entry has lastSyncAt ≥ end(14:03) + graceMin 30 = 14:33; the 14:40 pass → FINAL. Reasons: the verified rule adds no code; no allowlist in the grant, so allowlist.unchecked is not emitted; match.best {o2}; no cp.* (only address claims carry them).

Trap: without the first-seen rule o1 is a candidate with tp 1 and subject 1 → 1/1, and would be the best (VERIFIED 1/1 on o1). o1 is an orphan (inside the covered interval, assigned to no claim) with no activity → no attribution → no receipt (§7).
